reviewMethod: Original local reference files viewed at original image detail before implementation; no reference image was edited or bundled as an app-screen background.

supportedElements: Full-width white product rows with small rounded thumbnails, semibold title, secondary variant and unit price, and right-aligned multiplicative quantity.
Dark full-width Fulfill items action below product rows.
Bracketed store name and new-order notification body format.
implementationLimits: The marketing banner obscures the order header and is scaled outside the phone; its geometry is not used as iOS banner evidence.
Product title, price, symbol and quantity come from saved local order snapshots. Aggregate legacy orders retain an unnamed Custom order row.
Reference product photos are not redistributed. Catalog thumbnails remain user-selected SF Symbols.
Customer, payment and archive sections are local app scaffolding; this reference does not establish their exact layout or interaction.
No shipment address or shipping charge is invented where the saved order has no such fields.

supportedElements: Black Orders header over a white rounded body, circular search/location/sort/filter controls, status pills and grouped date headers.
Order row hierarchy of number and total, customer and count/time, and small fulfillment/payment badges.
implementationLimits: Oversized floating Fulfilled and Paid badges, shipping label, hardware and lower poster fade are marketing annotations.
The current saved model does not have shipping-method metadata. A universal Free Shipping claim has been removed from local rows.
Order creation with catalog products is a native local form; no public reference establishes the complete merchant create-order flow.

supportedElements: White rounded product card with thumbnail, name and price, gray capsule minus/count/plus control, green checked status and dark review action.
implementationLimits: The implementation adapts the pictured card to manual inventory adjustment and review. It does not pretend a barcode was scanned.
No camera, barcode lookup, order picking or warehouse integrations are implied.
Inventory edits save through the authoritative local commerce profile API. The native review screen is local scaffolding, not a referenced full-screen match.

unreferencedLocalFlows: Notification configuration, template loading and cue saving use native SwiftUI forms and the existing local scheduler. Their UI is not established by these public screenshots.
Scheduled notifications preserve store totals and are targeted to the selected commerce scene; iOS supplies the installed app identity.
The existing Pulse recommendation uses local order and inventory state. Public posters do not establish all assistant conversations, actions or animated states.
fidelityClaim: Reference-grounded visible portions and functional local actions; no complete app or pixel parity claim.
